statement: Let O = {(i,j) | 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = 1}. For S subset of O, let flip(S) be the matrix obtained from grid by changing exactly the cells in S to 0 and changing no other cell. A matrix is well-isolated if no two distinct 1-cells (i,j),(i',j') in it satisfy |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1. Let F = { |S| | S subset of O and flip(S) is well-isolated }. The function returns a result r and r = min F. (F is nonempty because S = O is valid.)
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail, panic, or overflow).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let k be the number of cells (i,j) with grid[i][j] = 1. The function returns a result r and 0 <= r <= floor(k/2).
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: The function returns a result r and r = 0 if and only if grid is well-isolated, i.e., there do not exist distinct cells (i,j),(i',j') with grid[i][j] = 1, grid[i'][j'] = 1, and |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let O = {(i,j) | 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = 1}. Two distinct cells (i,j),(i',j') in O are adjacent when |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1. The function returns a result r and r equals the maximum cardinality of a set M of unordered pairs {u,v} such that u and v are adjacent cells of O and no cell of O occurs in more than one pair of M.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let O = {(i,j) | 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = 1}. The function returns a result r and r equals the minimum cardinality of a set C subset of O such that for every two distinct cells u=(i,j), v=(i',j') in O with |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1, at least one of u and v belongs to C.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let O = {(i,j) | 0 <= i < m, 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] = 1} and let k = |O|. Let alpha be the maximum cardinality of a set I subset of O such that no two distinct cells of I are 4-directionally adjacent (i.e., for any (i,j),(i',j') in I, |i-i'| + |j-j'| != 1). The function returns a result r and r = k - alpha.

statement: Let rA and rB be the results returned by the function on A and B respectively. Then rA <= rB.
preconditions: Let A and B be two inputs satisfying the same rectangular-binary preconditions, with the same dimensions m,n, and A[i][j] <= B[i][j] for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: Let T be the n-by-m matrix defined by T[j][i] = grid[i][j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Let r be the result returned by the function on grid and let rT be the result returned on T. Then r = rT.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The input satisfies: 1 <= m <= 300; there exists n with 1 <= n <= 300 such that for every i with 0 <= i < m, len(grid[i]) = n; and for every i with 0 <= i < m and j with 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] is either 0 or 1.

statement: Let the maximal contiguous runs of 1s in the single row grid[0][0..n-1] have lengths L_1,...,L_q, where q >= 0 and each run is a maximal interval of columns whose entries are all 1. The function returns a result r and r = sum_{t=1..q} floor(L_t/2).

statement: Let R be the m-by-n matrix obtained by reversing the rows of grid: R[i][j] = grid[m-1-i][j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Let r be the result returned by the function on grid and let rR be the result returned on R. Then r = rR.

statement: If grid[i][j] = 1 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, then the function returns a result r and r = floor(m*n/2).

statement: Let E be the number of unordered pairs { (i,j),(i',j') } of cells such that grid[i][j] = 1, grid[i'][j'] = 1, and |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1. The function returns a result r and r <= E.
